item.title: THE LONG EXHALE | A GROUP EXHIBITION — Fri Aug 21, 5:00 PM — 5 Points Gallery
item.description:
5 Points Gallery is pleased to present The Long Exhale, bringing together work by the ten artists of 5 Points Gallery. As the pace of summer begins to soften, The Long Exhale invites visitors to pause, look closely, and linger. The exhibition offers a refreshing mix of painting, sculpture, fused glass, mixed media, and finely crafted furniture, with each artist offering a distinct creative perspective. Join us for the Opening Reception on Friday, August 21, 2026, from 6–9 pm to meet the artists. The exhibition runs from August 20 through September 12, 2026. Visit 5 Points Gallery in person or online at https://5pointsgallery.com. All work from the exhibition is available for shipping or pickup. Gallery hours: Thursdays and Fridays 5–9pm and Saturdays 1–9pm. Artists are available to talk about their work. For a private viewing, contact us at info@5pointsgallery.com.

item.title: Downtown Durham African American Historian-Guided Tour — Sat Aug 22, 4:00 PM — CCB Plaza
item.description:
Durham: the mecca of black capitalism and the center of North Carolina’s African American business community. Join a local historian on this guided walking tour of Durham’s Black Wall Street, hearing the stories of how a humble sharecropper became the owner of the largest black-ned company in American history, and seeing some of the sites related to their stories. Learn how businessmen, labor organizers, educated academics, and craftsmen each contributed to the unique history of Durham’s African American community.

item.title: Info Session: NIH Loan Repayment Programs for Health Professionals (LRP) — Wed Aug 26, 11:00 AM — Virtual
item.description:
Are you a biomedical or biobehavioral PhD researcher? Did you know that the National Institutes of Health (NIH) will help pay back your student loans? You're invited to an in-depth overview of the NIH Loan Repayment Program from the Division of Loan Repayment Director, Matthew Lockhart MBA. The NIH Loan Repayment Program (LRPs) are a set of programs established by Congress designed to recruit and retain highly qualified health professionals into biomedical or biobehavioral research centers. The NIH LRPs pay up to $50,000 annually of qualified educational debt in return for a commitment to engage in NIH mission-relevant research.
Applicants must hold a PhD, MD, PharmD, DVM, or equivalent doctoral-level degree and must be a US citizen or permanent resident. The NIH LRPs will accept applications from Sept 1-Nov 19, 2026. Don't miss your opportunity to learn how you could receive up to $100,000 in educational debt relief!

item.title: MEMS Distinguished Seminar: Tim Lieuwen, "Patterns and Structure in the Fury and Noise: Coherent Structures and Organized Dynamics in Modern Power Systems." — Wed Aug 26, 12:00 PM — Fitzpatrick Center Schiciano Auditorium Side A
item.description:
The Thomas Lord Department of Mechanical Engineering & Materials Science hosts Professor Tim Lieuwen (Georgia Tech) to present the MEMS Distinguished Seminar, "Patterns and Structure in the Fury and Noise: Coherent Structures and Organized Dynamics in Modern Power Systems."
ABSTRACT: Future propulsion and power systems will be profoundly shaped by societal drivers including decarbonization, national security, and resilience. Addressing these challenges also motivates a rich set of fundamental problems in fluid mechanics and combustion. The internal flows of aircraft engines and power plants, for example, exhibit fascinating and beautiful instabilities-phenomena that are scientifically compelling in their own right. This talk will discuss the mechanisms leading to self-organized behaviors in these systems. It will span from fundamentals to current applications and unsolved problems at the intersection of combustion, fluid mechanics, and flow stability.

item.title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star (Theatre for the Very Young) — Fri Aug 28, 10:00 AM — Raleigh Little Theatre
item.description:
Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star is an interactive children’s theatre piece for very young audiences, performed by two Star Keepers named Glimmer and Sparkle. It’s time for the night sky to fill with stars, but one important star — Little Star, the wishing star — is missing because Sparkle rushed through putting the stars away the previous morning and muddled everything up. What follows is a search-and-rescue adventure as the two star keepers (and the audience) hunt for Little Star, discovering along the way that all the other stars have been put in the wrong places too and need to be moved to their proper place. Audience members help the Star Keepers find and re-organize the sky just in time for nightfall so that everyone can make a wish on their favorite star. Twinkle, Twinkle explores the ideas that mistakes happen, feelings are valid, and no one has to face hard things alone – all wrapped up in a genuinely joyful romp about stars.
By Ernie Nolan Produced by special arrangemen

item.title: Science TODAY: When Wild Animals Meet People — Tue Sep 1, 11:30 AM — Nature Research Center
item.description:
Understanding Human-Carnivore Conflict in China Go inside the globe of the SECU Daily Planet Theater for live presentations and interactive shows led by scientists and educators. Meet researchers, witness live demonstrations, and engage in Q&A sessions with experts. With ever-changing topics and guests, there’s always something new and exciting to learn. Today’s Topic What happens when people and large carnivores share the same landscape? Using 520 reported conflict events across China, this talk explores where conflicts occur, why they happen, and how people and wildlife can coexist. Today’s Expert Jiahui Yuan, Tsinghua University & Biodiversity lab, North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences.

item.title: Luminary & Freedom Stories — Fri Sep 18, 7:00 PM — Bennett Place State Historic Site
item.description:
During this special luminary program, Bennett Place invites you to reflect on the end of the Civil War as a momentous step towards freedom for all Americans and the end of chattel slavery in the United States.
Walk among 3,310 luminaries - one for every 1,000 enslaved people in North Carolina - and reflect on experiences of enslavement and freedom. Historians dot the path and share stories of people's pathways to freedom and life after slavery & the Civil War.
--
Harriet Ann Daves recalled just how monumental Civil War surrenders were for her family: "When the surrender came my grandfather came to my mother and told her: 'Well, you are as free as I am.'"
Claiming freedom was not so straightforward for the 331,059 enslaved women, children, and men during the Civil War. Some took enormous risk to reach Union lines before the federal government made any promise of abolishing slavery. Others left their homes and plantations to follow Sherman's army as they marched through the southeast

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Thu Nov 19 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Thu Nov 19, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources
